newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Cultus sees Tenacious as future producer.
newsitem.headline: Cultus sees Tenacious as future producer.

text.p: Cultus Petroleum NL said on Monday it is suspending its Tenacious-1 well in the Timor Sea offshore Western Australia as a potential future producer after it encountered a 39.5 metre gross oil column.
Cultus said the Tenacious-1 sidetrack well flowed at 7,667 barrels of approximately 49 degree API oil and 4.02 million cubic feet of gas a day through a one-and-a-half inch choke.
Analysts said the well was a good result in an area that has seen a great deal of exploration since the discovery of the Jabiru and Challis oilfields.

"The industry has spent probably in excess of a billion dollars since the early 1980s looking for oil and gas in that region and basically has not been successful," said James Capel oil and gas analyst Mario Traviati.
It was the first time oil had been found in Tithonian sands in the area, and the site was near existing infrastructure at Jabiru/Chalice, Traviati said.
Cultus said the joint venturers would analyse the results at Tenacious with a view to choosing sites for further drilling.
The AC/P17 permit joint venture is held equally by operator Cultus, Cosmo Oil Co unit Cosmo Oil Ashmore Ltd, Gulf Canada unit Gulf (Aust) Resources Ltd, and PanCanadian Resources Ltd.
Cultus shares were 10 cents higher at A$3.90 at 12.05 p.m. (0204 GMT).
